# clio auth token revoke

Remove the record; the running MCP HTTP server stops accepting it without a restart, and the sync server applies the change at its next start

## Usage

```
clio auth token revoke --label LABEL [--output json|text]
```

## Description

removes the record; the running MCP HTTP server applies the change without a restart, while the sync server applies it at its next start; the write holds the store lock, so it never drops a record a concurrent add wrote, and --db, --backend, --actor, and --bank are refused

## Options

| Option | Kind | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--label LABEL` | text |  | Names the credential record that `auth_cli` adds or revokes; it is the record's identity. |
| `--output json\|text` | enum: json, text |  | Selects the output mode that `cli_output::resolve_output` returns; the terminal decides it when absent. |

## Global options

| Option | Kind | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--no-input` |  |  | Refuses interactive input; `backup_restore_cli` treats a run with it as non-interactive. |
| `--yes` |  |  | Answers yes to the destructive-confirmation gate that `cli_confirm::confirmed` applies. |

## Examples

Remove one credential record.
```
clio auth token revoke --label laptop
```

Remove one record and report as JSON.
```
clio auth token revoke --label laptop -o json
```
